raw_response:
I’ve farmed here a long time, so I’m not going to make big changes just because somebody says a new way is better. On my 40 mu, I’ll still keep most of the land in the wheat-maize rotation, because that gives steadier grain income, and I’ll keep some cotton because if grain price is weak, cotton can still help the household cash flow. I only have two people at home, so I can’t spread myself too thin with labor-heavy management. For wheat, I’ll put a bit more attention on base fertilizer and make sure I irrigate at the key stages, because if wheat stand is weak in spring it’s hard to make up later. For maize, the turnaround after wheat is tight, so I’ll keep tillage simple and plant quickly after harvest. For cotton, I won’t push inputs too high, because cotton takes more labor and the return is less certain than before, but I’ll still keep enough fertilizer and water so it doesn’t fall off too much. I usually look at what worked on my own fields first, then what the better farmers nearby are doing, and if the extension people say something reasonable, I adjust a little, not too much.
